verdict.rationale: Buzz is an open-source codebase that a team can run on its own relay with no external services, so there is no vendor-imposed paid tier gating message history. History is searchable, with agents searching 'six months of history'. However, no pricing tier or retention policy is documented, so free use with unlimited history is only implied by self-hosting. Missing for 10: an explicit free-tier or pricing definition, a documented message-history retention policy with no cap, terms for operator-hosted plans, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a team-admin, I can keep my team on a free tier without losing access to older message history

citations.quote: Run your own relay for one community, or let an operator host thousands on shared infrastructure — same OSS codebase
Agents search six months of history and post the threads, not vibes.
